plan.question: Does learning get better as the company has more history? (scaling check)
plan.world: data/worlds/full_seed20261104 (demo world), company T01; records 2026-08-01 to 2026-10-29
plan.arms: history length 30, 60, 90 days: records cut at the end of 2026-08-30, 2026-09-29, 2026-10-29; company 'today' = the day after the cutoff (90 days = the live path unchanged)
plan.pipeline: digest (5 digests, as digest.build) -> miner.mine with Muse Spark 1.3 on the Meta API, temperature 0 -> evidence gate (store.add_proposals) checking against the same cut records; each run into an empty store
plan.repeats: 3 per length (9 mining calls), order rep0: 30,60,90; rep1: 30,60,90; rep2: 30,60,90
plan.scoring: evaluate.score unchanged (EXP-008/009b): passed = CANDIDATE, NEEDS_EVIDENCE or EXPIRED; recall = hidden learnable rules found / learnable rules over all 90 days (fixed denominator); precision = passed lessons matching a non-trap hidden rule / passed; traps = trap rules (habit, contradiction, look_alike, one_off, cold_chain) among passed lessons

bar.B1: mean recall at 90 days >= mean recall at 30 days (fixed denominator, mean over the 3 repeats)
bar.B2: precision at 90 days >= 0.85, pooled over the 3 repeats (true passed / passed)
bar.B3: 0 trap rules admitted in every run at every length
bar.verdict: met only if B1, B2 and B3 are all met; a miss is reported as a miss

plan.reported_not_judged: 60 days; recall against only the rules with any evidence by the cutoff (same learnable definition as evaluate.Truth, restricted to records up to the cutoff); rules found per length; proposals, passed, false lessons; digest size; cost
plan.partial: if the budget stops the run, only lengths with at least one completed repeat are judged and the result is labelled partial
plan.budget: hard cap $1.50 total Meta spend: 1 smoke call (30 days, not part of the result) + main run capped at $1.40 in the script (stops before a call that could pass it). Meta API only; baseten_api_key blanked.
plan.caveats: one company, one generated world, hidden rules from our own generator; temperature 0 so repeats measure only API nondeterminism; fewer rules have any evidence in 30 days, so fixed-denominator recall mixes 'not learnable yet' with 'missed'; the visible-by-cutoff recall separates them.
